Over the past 15 years, the situation regarding human, indigenous and environmental rights in Bolivia has deteriorated significantly. The country is in the midst of a severe, multifaceted crisis that continues to worsen. The presidential election marks the end of nearly two decades of left-wing government. The new president, Paz, stands for a course of structural reforms and the promotion of extractive activities to boost the economy, which is likely to further worsen respect for environmental and human rights.
